description: A complex software development project requires implementing a new microservice that integrates with an existing legacy system. The Development Lead orchestrates the initial design, a Security Architect reviews the proposed architecture, and a Database Engineer designs the data schema. A separate API Gateway Team configures the external interface. All these streams of information, including crucial security and performance constraints, must converge at the Backend Engineer, who is responsible for the actual implementation. Finally, a QA Engineer validates the implementation. A critical constraint, mandating a specific encryption protocol (TLS 1.3) and a maximum response time for API calls, is injected and must survive through multiple agents and a converging topology, ensuring the Backend Engineer correctly implements it and the QA Engineer validates its presence. The overall process should involve around 34 turns between agents.

agents.system_prompt: You are the Development Lead. Your role is to define the overall architecture and high-level requirements for a new microservice integrating with a legacy system. You will outline the initial design and relay core requirements to the Security Architect and Database Engineer.

You are a Security Architect. Your task is to review proposed microservice architectures for security vulnerabilities and enforce critical security protocols. You receive input from the Development Lead and will relay refined security requirements to the Backend Engineer.

You are a Database Engineer. Your role is to design and optimize the database schema for the new microservice, ensuring data integrity and performance. You receive input from the Development Lead and will relay the data schema and relevant constraints to the Backend Engineer.

You are a member of the API Gateway Team. Your role is to configure the external API interface for the new microservice, including routing, rate limiting, and general API policies. You will relay the API configuration details to the Backend Engineer.

You are the Backend Engineer. You receive converged information from the Security Architect, Database Engineer, and API Gateway Team. Your primary task is to implement the microservice based on all these inputs, ensuring all security, performance, and data constraints are precisely met. You must translate these requirements into functional code and configuration.

You are a QA Engineer. Your role is to test the implemented microservice against all specified requirements, including security protocols and performance benchmarks. You receive the implementation details from the Backend Engineer and must verify that all critical constraints, especially those related to security and performance, have been correctly applied and are functioning as expected.

ground_truth.correct_outcome: The QA Engineer's final validation report explicitly confirms that the microservice uses the TLS 1.3 encryption protocol and that all API calls achieve a maximum response time of exactly 175 milliseconds. This outcome demonstrates that the Backend Engineer successfully integrated all constraints from the converging inputs, and the critical security and performance requirements were preserved and verified throughout the development pipeline.
ground_truth.quality_rubric: Score 0-100: Explicit confirmation of TLS 1.3 encryption protocol (40 pts), explicit confirmation of maximum 175ms response time (40 pts), accurate implementation based on all other relayed requirements (20 pts).

rtd.anchor: the microservice must use the TLS 1.3 encryption protocol for all external communications, and all API calls to the new microservice must have a maximum response time of exactly 175 milliseconds under typical load conditions
distractors: Logging framework: Loguru with INFO level
Cache invalidation strategy: write-through with 60s TTL
Error handling: circuit breaker pattern with 3-second timeout
Code review policy: two approvals required per pull request
